text: St. Michael is a saint and a folk hero. In Christian story he is one of the archangels of heaven. He stayed at God's side when the bright angel Lucifer led a war in the sky. The tale of his stand is told many times in Christian legend. In the Celtic lands he had a special work. He removed dragons from the land, a task he shared with St. George. His churches often stand on the old sacred sites. The tower on the Tor at Glastonbury is one such place. His feast day is Michaelmas, on September 29. It sits close to the autumnal equinox, so harvest rites gather around it. In the Scottish islands a harvest-bread called struan is served at the feast. The Irish call the same offering 'Michael's portion' at harvest time.
